Hi Sophie / Acme ops,

We observed a regional degradation impacting our inference edge nodes in EU and APAC starting ~02:45 UTC. The symptom set: increased tail latency and intermittent 5xx for customers routing through certain peering exchanges. The Root Cause Investigation is ongoing with our infra partner (copied).

Immediate actions we've taken (status):
- Automatic traffic steering to US region for affected routes — in progress (partial).
- Temporarily increased replica capacity on US and select EU control-plane nodes — done.
- Enabled graceful throttling for very long-sequence requests to avoid KV-cache storms — done.

Recommended immediate customer actions (so you have clear next steps):
1) If you have region pins, consider temporarily disabling EU/APAC pinning to allow failover to US endpoints.
2) If latency-sensitive requests exist, change your client to prefer low-latency endpoints (see attached traffic-mapping.csv for domain -> region mapping).
3) Review any hard-coded DNS TTLs — lowering to 30s will help faster convergence while we complete the fix.

We're treating this with high priority and will share a post-incident summary once we confirm the fix and the mitigation timeline.

Ben / Sophie / team,

Short answers to Sophie's questions:
- Data residency: Customer payloads are encrypted in transit and for customers using Redwood Private or Dedicated we maintain keys in-region. For hosted API customers (like Acme Bank), request routing to a different region means data packets cross borders; we will include a full summary of what metadata and payloads crossed in the postmortem. For immediate compliance workarounds, we can enable encrypted payload proxying and a minimized header mode; Laura will outline the client config.
- Steering extension: We've started extending steering to two additional US POPs (us-west-2 and us-east-1) — this reduced 5xx by ~40% in our tests. We will need to temporarily increase per-tenant burst limits by 20% to prevent throttling during the migration (ETA 60 minutes).

Evidence collection: I will pull peering logs and KV eviction logs and drop them in the linked drive. Ops note: please avoid reattaching previous capture files to customer emails — provide a redacted summary and attach full evidence to the secure drive link.

Subject: Post-incident update & customer action checklist — APAC/EU edge disruption (draft)

Hi Sophie — apologies again for the disruption. Below is a concise summary and an action checklist we recommend for Acme Bank. We're attaching a draft internal postmortem and a csv mapping of domains to region endpoints for your ops team.

Summary (what happened)
- Timeline: Initial signal at ~02:45 UTC May 5; partial mitigation (steering + replica increases) reduced errors by May 6 06:30 UTC; full traffic normalization to standard routing occurred May 7 14:00 UTC after fixes rolled to peering config.
- Root cause (short): A bad BGP policy change at a major peering exchange caused asymmetric routing and overloaded a subset of our EU/APAC edge nodes. That in turn caused KV-cache pressure and increased tail latency.
- Impact: Many EU requests and a subset of APAC long-sequence workloads experienced elevated p99 latency and intermittent 5xx; US region remained within SLOs.

Customer action checklist (recommended):
1) If you require strict data residency, confirm whether you want us to route EU-origin traffic back to EU-only endpoints once traffic stabilizes — we can pin flows but this may increase latency while we finish remediation.
2) For immediate resilience: enable client-side failover to redwood-us-1.region.redwood.com and reduce DNS TTLs to 30s for the next 48 hours (see config-snippet.txt).
3) Pause non-essential long-sequence batch jobs in APAC for 24 hours.
4) Review the attached traffic-mapping.csv and flag any domains that must be excluded from cross-region steering.

What we're delivering to Acme (next steps):
- By May 8 EOD: redacted evidence package (peering logs, eviction logs) and a customer-facing postmortem PDF.
- By May 9: recommended long-term controls — BGP policy detection alarms, improved KV-cache backpressure handling, and expanded cross-POP failover testing.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf (internal draft), traffic-mapping.csv, config-snippet.txt

Please reply if you'd like us to open an emergency maintenance window for your customers; we can coordinate language and timing.

Thanks for your patience — we take this seriously and will follow through with both the technical fix and compliance evidence.
